clue.text: In order to fill pit? You'd need to hear of advanced decay

indicators.note: the solver must hear how the phrase built from these words sounds, not see how it is spelt

parts.note: an order is a decree; split it to take pit as its filling, then add you'd, and say the whole run aloud

explanation.surface: Someone filling in a hole is warned about a serious state of rot.
explanation.walkthrough: DECREE is split by PIT ('to fill'), then YOU'D follows; 'hear of' says that DECRE-PIT-YOU'D, spoken, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepitude is the worn-out, broken-down state of old age, a synonym for advanced decay.

clue.text: Flat can be divided

definitions.meaning: a whole number that splits exactly into two equal halves

explanation.surface: A level surface that can be split up.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means level and smooth, and an even number is one that splits by two without remainder.

clue.text: Part given to a model, for example

definitions.text: given to a model, for example
definitions.meaning: the word attached to model in the phrase for a person others look up to

explanation.surface: An actor's part handed to a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is an actor's part, and the word precedes 'model' in the idiom for someone admired and copied.

clue.text: Inclined to give a chum the paintings I kept…

indicators.note: the chum is said to keep the paintings and I, so they sit inside

parts.note: a pal is a chum
paintings are art
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keen to hand a friend the pictures they were holding on to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined to' reads as willingness to give, but 'Inclined' alone is the definition and 'to give a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be partial to something is to be fond of or biased towards it, a synonym for inclined.

clue.text: ..in apartment at eaton square

annotationWithheld.why: ..in apartment at eaton square (4): the hidden TATE is plain, but the definition is the 'paintings I kept' of 4-down, carried over by the ellipsis, so this clue has no defining words of its own

clue.text: An area divided by religion

parts.note: reads like a region split by sectarian strife, but means a district marked out by a church as the patch of one bishop

explanation.surface: A region torn apart by religious conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocese is a bishop's district, a territory into which the church carves up the land.

clue.text: Island's cereal production on a sound footing

indicators.note: the word sound tells the solver the cereal is wanted for how it is said

parts.note: barley is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: An island's grain harvest is well established.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent BARLEY is said 'bah-lee', so 'on a sound footing' turns it into BALI. 'Island's' stands for 'island is'; 'production' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island, an example of an island.

clue.text: He was always illuminating

parts.note: reads as praise for a man who was ever enlightening, but means one whose job was lighting street lamps

explanation.surface: A tribute to a man who always shed light on things.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamplighter was the worker who lit gas street lamps each evening, so his trade was literally to illuminate.

clue.text: Army following up lawyer's information

indicators.note: the army comes after the lawyer, so it is written second

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: Soldiers tracking down a lawyer's facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures, a synonym for information.

clue.text: Notes to Clara turned into a written affirmation

parts.note: D and E are two musical notes
taken as written

indicators.note: the word into is turned about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone writes musical notes for Clara and they become a formal statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes to Clara' looks like a letter to a woman, but the notes are musical ones; 'turned' works only on the word that follows it, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A declaration is a formal statement, often written and signed, so a synonym for a written affirmation.

clue.text: Stumble, but I'm a record-breaker all the same!

indicators.note: I'm breaks into the record, splitting it open

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner who trips yet still claims to have set a new record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record-breaker' looks like a sporting boast, but only its second half is the signal, telling I'm to break into the record.
explanation.definitionFit: To limp is to walk unevenly, much like stumbling along.

clue.text: When these two birds get together, one disappears

definitions.text: When these two birds get together, one disappears

parts.words: When these two birds get together, one disappears
parts.note: the two birds' names joined make a single bird of prey, and when that hunter meets the smaller one it is eaten

explanation.surface: A riddle about two birds meeting and one vanishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrowhawk is a small bird of prey that hunts songbirds, and its name joins a small bird to a raptor.

clue.text: It can give rail that extra edge

definitions.text: It can give rail that extra edge

parts.words: It can give rail that extra edge
parts.note: sounds like a competitive advantage, but means a projecting lip on a wheel that keeps it on the track

explanation.surface: Something that gives a railway company a competitive advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A flange is a projecting rim, such as the one on a train wheel that grips the inside of the track.

clue.text: An arctic tiger? No, a smaller predator

parts.note: the North Pole is in the Arctic
a tiger is a big cat

explanation.surface: Asking whether a big cat lives in the far north, then correcting to a smaller hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An arctic tiger?' is a mock suggestion: a polar big cat, POLE + CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a small carnivore of the weasel family that hunts rodents and rabbits.

clue.text: You could make a fortune with this!

definitions.text: You could make a fortune with this!

parts.words: You could make a fortune with this!
parts.note: reads like a get-rich promise, but means foretelling the future with a deck of cards

explanation.surface: A sales pitch promising riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot cards are used by fortune tellers to read a person's future.

clue.text: One weapon used for ages is a chopper

indicators.note: the words are chopped up, so their letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient weapon described as a blade for cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' looks like the definition but chops up AGES IS A; 'used for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa, one kind of weapon.

clue.text: Broken seat's a valuable item

indicators.note: a broken seat is in pieces, so its letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: here the apostrophe S counts as a letter, giving five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A damaged chair turns out to be worth something.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something owned that has worth, a synonym for a valuable item.

clue.text: What the Scots call garlic!

parts.note: suggests Scots dialect for a pungent bulb, but plays on the name of the Highland language sounding like the vegetable

explanation.surface: A claim about the Scottish word for a cooking ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Scottish pronunciation, the language of the Highlands is said 'gah-lik', just like the bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaelic is the Celtic language of the Scottish Highlands and islands, the tongue Scots speakers call their own.

clue.text: In a perverse way, a failure may almost please

indicators.note: perverse means contrary or twisted, so the letters are rearranged
almost the whole word, so it loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A slip-up that might nearly prove pleasing, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PLEASE to PLEAS, and 'In a perverse way' rearranges that; 'may' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or brief failure, as in a lapse of concentration.

clue.text: A new variation in the mating season — just a little one

indicators.note: N goes inside the season as a small variation on it

parts.note: the rut is the breeding season of deer

explanation.surface: A new twist during the breeding season produces only a tiny offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A runt is the smallest animal of a litter, the little one of the brood.

clue.text: Network wants me? Don't say a word!

parts.note: taken as written
sh is the sound made to ask for silence

explanation.surface: A computer network wants you but asks you to keep quiet about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is an interlaced structure of threads or links, a network.

clue.text: Leaks from ozone — less nitrogen, more sun

indicators.note: the answer is made from the letters of the gas, reworked

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
S is the abbreviation for sun, as in Sunday

explanation.surface: Something seeps out of the ozone layer as nitrogen falls and sunshine rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' takes N from OZONE to leave OZOE, which 'from' rearranges; S is then added on the end ('more').
explanation.definitionFit: To ooze is to seep out slowly, as a fluid leaks through a gap.

clue.text: On the pitch, I love taking Canadians' part

parts.note: taken as written
tar is black pitch
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A cricketer on the pitch claims to love joining a Canadian team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link; 'pitch' looks like a sports field but is the black sticky stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is one of Canada's provinces, a part of the country.

clue.text: A port made in Italy

parts.note: suggests a fortified wine produced by Italians, but means a harbour town on the Italian coast

explanation.surface: An Italian-made bottle of fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno is a seaport city on Italy's south-west coast.

clue.text: Active use of music by stately home owners

indicators.note: the owners stand beside the music, written after it

parts.note: opera is a form of music
NT is the National Trust, the British charity that owns many country houses

explanation.surface: Music being performed at a country house run by a heritage charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Operant means operating or functioning, so active.

clue.text: Touchy-feely performance which may floor outsider!

indicators.note: the floor covering stands outside the performance, around it

parts.note: a tile is something that can floor a room
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: An emotional show that could knock out an underdog contender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' looks like a verb meaning knock down, but 'which may floor' describes a floor covering; 'outsider' says that covering wraps round the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to touch, so a tactile person is fond of physical contact.

clue.text: Tramp seen in Soho bookstore

indicators.note: the answer can be seen inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A vagrant spotted in a bookshop in London's Soho district.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a lively district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is a homeless wanderer, a synonym for tramp.

clue.text: Make a dash for the bar

definitions.meaning: a sliding bar that fastens a door

explanation.surface: Run for the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to run off suddenly, and a bolt is a metal bar sliding to lock a door.

clue.text: Getting strung-out at home…

parts.note: suggests a drug user at home, but means yarn being drawn out into thread at a domestic spinning wheel

explanation.surface: Someone getting high at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun describes fibre drawn and twisted into thread, as done on a spinning wheel in the home.

clue.text: It's volcanic, but can produce neat work

indicators.note: the word neat is worked over, so its letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A volcano that turns out tidy work.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily.

clue.text: A giver of heavenly parties?

parts.note: suggests someone who throws wonderful parties, but also hints at the heavenly army of angels

explanation.surface: Praise for someone whose parties are divine.
explanation.definitionFit: A host gives parties, and the heavenly host is the biblical army of angels.

clue.text: Readiness to make an allowance for homework

indicators.note: the allowance comes after the homework, so it is written second

parts.note: prep is school homework in British boarding-school slang
an gives the letter A
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: Being ready to give a pupil a little extra time for homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link. PREP is the boarding-school word for homework done in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparation is the state of being ready, so readiness.

clue.text: Wish to leave paper? Over my dead body!

definitions.text: leave paper? Over my dead body!
definitions.meaning: a document of bequests, which only takes effect over one's dead body

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to hand over a document until they die.
explanation.definitionFit: Will means desire, and a will is the legal document that disposes of property after death.

clue.text: Sensible — like a fox heading for cover

definitions.text: like a fox heading for cover
definitions.meaning: a fox's den is called an earth, and it heads downwards into it

explanation.surface: A practical fox makes for shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Down-to-earth means practical and realistic; a hunted fox goes to ground in its den, an earth.
